Enterprise GEO platform

What is Adobe Brand Visibility (ABV)?

ABV connects the full GEO loop

Generative engine optimization (GEO) helps you improve how your brand is found, described, and cited in AI answers.

ABV is designed to be the best enterprise GEO tool, uniquely connecting the full loop end to end:

set a business goal and baseline prioritize and deploy improvements verify what went live measure impact and choose the next action

GEO builds on SEO. Keep your search foundations; add AI visibility, answer quality, and business-outcome measurement to the workflow.

One workflow, two layers

How ABV brings Semrush and Adobe together

Semrush · Market intelligence

Choose the right focus

Semrush Enterprise AIO brings market and competitor context. Narrow broad prompt demand to a relevant, stable cohort aligned with one business goal.

Adobe · Optimization

Deploy changes and validate

Track Brand Presence, prioritize work in Opportunity Workspace, and deploy through Optimize at Edge or your publishing process. Validate what went live.

Together · One ABV workflow

Run the complete GEO loop

Combine Semrush intelligence and Adobe optimization: set a business goal, curate prompts, baseline, plan, deploy and validate, then evaluate results and business impact to decide next.

Staggered, not stacked. Offset starts to spread implementation and review work. Every loop keeps its own business goal, stable prompt cohort, baseline, and owner; each readout informs the next scope.

Every loop follows the same six steps

  1. 01

    Frame

    Agree on the business goal, audience, scope, owner, and success measures.

  2. 02

    Curate

    Select a relevant, stable prompt cohort for the focus area.

  3. 03

    Baseline

    Record starting visibility and business measures before changes.

  4. 04

    Plan

    Prioritize actions, assign owners, and confirm approvals.

  5. 05

    Implement

    Deploy supported changes and validate what went live.

  6. 06

    Review

    Measure results and business impact; note limits and decide next.

Start with one complete loop. Add parallel loops when publishing and review capacity are ready. The full GEO loop guide explains the end-to-end method at a high level.

Product architecture

From configured inputs to insight and action

Brand and prompt configuration, site evidence, and connected analytics feed ABV insights and optimization. Each workflow uses the inputs it needs.

Inputs · Scope and evidence

Set the scope

Brands, markets, domains, and tracked prompts define monitoring. CDN logs add agent requests and human referrals; supported analytics connections add business outcomes. Connect only what the workflow requires.

Analysis · Distinct signals

Find what to investigate

Prompt responses inform Brand Presence; site and traffic analysis inform URL investigation and opportunities. Keep mentions, citations, agent requests, and human referrals distinct—not one combined score.

Action · Two delivery routes

Route approved work

Opportunities proposes changes; Workspace coordinates owners and progress. Deliver supported agent-facing changes through Optimize at Edge; route other work through AEM/CMS, engineering, or offsite owners.

Insight is not delivery or impact. A recommendation or Workspace status proves neither. See the features guide for capabilities and the readiness guide for prerequisites.

Prompt strategy

Source and curate focused prompts

Semrush AI Visibility helps teams explore how brands and competitors appear in AI answers, uncover relevant topics, and discover prompts worth investigating. Use these insights to build a focused prompt set for ABV measurement.

Explore · AI Visibility

Find relevant opportunities

Use market and competitor insights to identify visibility gaps, emerging topics, and customer questions that can inform GEO priorities.

Plan · Prompt Strategy

Turn opportunities into focus

Use discovered prompts as a starting point. Refine them around the audience, intent, product or service, market, and business goal; remove duplicates and out-of-scope prompts.

Track · Brand Presence

Measure a defined prompt set

Select a balanced, stable cohort that reflects the goal and audience. Establish a baseline, then review visibility consistently as changes are made.

Use the views together: AI Visibility informs where to look; Prompt Strategy helps define what to track; Brand Presence follows the selected focus over time.

Where GEO work happens

Different levers support different visibility gaps

GEO can involve changes across your own content and technology, trusted sources elsewhere on the web, and—where relevant—your commerce experience. Choose the work based on the business goal and evidence; not every change belongs in ABV or follows the same delivery path.

Owned site · Content

Make key pages useful in answers

Strengthen the pages that address priority customer questions with clear, accurate, well-organized information.

  • Direct explanations, comparisons, and FAQs
  • Distinctive expertise and evidence
  • Consistent product, service, and policy details

Owned site · Technical

Make information accessible and dependable

Review the technical conditions that affect whether systems can reach, interpret, and reliably measure your content.

  • Crawl access, rendering, and page structure
  • Canonical URLs and appropriate structured data
  • Analytics or log integrations where they support measurement

Beyond your site · Off-site

Improve the wider information picture

AI answers can draw on sources beyond your domain. Work with the owners of relevant, credible sources to improve factual accuracy and consistency.

  • Publisher, partner, marketplace, and directory information
  • Reviews and other trusted third-party references
  • Earned coverage and corrections—not artificial mentions

Commerce · Adobe Commerce context

Clarify products and the buying journey

For commerce goals, make product information easy to understand and keep the path from discovery to purchase coherent.

  • Useful category and product descriptions
  • Accurate attributes, availability, pricing, and policies
  • Clear product data and a dependable storefront experience

How this connects to the next section: These workstreams may overlap, but they have different owners and implementation routes. Optimize at Edge is one supported route for approved agent-facing changes; it does not replace CMS, Commerce, engineering, or off-site work.

Optimize at Edge

Deliver approved optimizations to AI agents

Serve approved optimizations to routed AI agents without rewriting origin content or changing normal human and search-bot delivery.

Prepare · Routing

Configure the boundary

IT/CDN sets routing at the outermost CDN for selected paths and allows the AdobeEdgeOptimize/1.0 fetcher through applicable robots, WAF, and bot-management controls.

Apply · Approval

Review and deploy

Confirm enabled types—such as content recovery, summaries, or FAQs. Preview and refine where supported, then deploy the approved URLs and optimization type. Eligibility depends on the account.

Validate · Control

Verify live delivery

Check the optimized content served to routed agents, record deployment scope and date, and roll back when needed. Origin CMS content and normal human/search delivery remain unchanged.

Deployment does not guarantee uplift or an IME report. Confirm automatic-measurement support separately; otherwise evaluate against an agreed baseline. Routing and prerequisites.

Value by business goal

Match the funnel to your business goal

Discovery

Foundation + 01–02

Enter the category shortlist

For a product launch or priority market, make key pages accessible and improve presence on the prompts that matter.

Evidence to reviewReadable content, successful agent access, brand mentions, and visibility.

Trust

03–04

Be accurate and credible

For complex products or policy-sensitive content, improve factual representation and make authoritative pages easier to cite.

Evidence to reviewReviewed answer accuracy, sentiment, citations, and cited URLs.

Growth

05–06

Earn qualified engagement

For acquisition or commerce goals, connect visits from AI answers with useful engagement, leads, conversions, or revenue.

Evidence to reviewBaseline vs. post-deployment analytics and AI referrals; distinguish contribution from causal proof.

  • One goal per loopAgree on the business measure and the upstream signals needed to interpret it.
  • Fix the foundation firstGaps in access limit every layer above, so check them early.
  • Connect the evidenceAgentic Traffic needs CDN log forwarding. Business Impact needs connected Adobe Analytics, CJA, or GA4 and entitlement.

Summary

From GEO insight to impact.

  • See the opportunity

    GEO improves how brands appear in AI answers. ABV combines Semrush insights with Adobe optimization and measurement.

  • Choose the right levers

    Improve on-site content, technical foundations, off-site sources, or—where relevant—Adobe Commerce experiences.

  • Route changes appropriately

    Use Optimize at Edge for supported agent-facing changes; other work follows the relevant team’s process.

  • Close the loop

    Set a goal and baseline, validate changes, assess results and evidence limits, then choose what comes next.
